notes: The previous v18 release was archived before editing on archive/pre-level3-feedback-v18 at 25bc397aec1bad90158f318d1a0efbfd6a953509. Existing historical archives, reports and numbered ZIPs are preserved.

All small editor-question headings have been removed. The all-covered first result now asks Can new weights make Alex go further? Optional hints are shorter and no longer constrained to a 570px text column. Browser checks establish a single desktop line while allowing narrow layouts to wrap without overflow.

The redundant editor allocation strip and 100% allocated label are removed. Positive weight validation, exact total 100, native slider bounds, confirmation order, linked final pair and manual publication/observation are unchanged.

Last observation retains each actual effort band and adds an amber warning-icon reminder: Stopped after earning the marks he wanted. This describes the existing stopping observation across distributions and does not label shared attention as failure or assert that another split necessarily solves the stopping rule.

The reported Focus/Reflection/Peer response route 49/26/25 is browser checked with three steady bands, the simplified question, visible stopping concern and one-line desktop hint. At 49/27/24, the last task still changes to minimum and Less effort under the unchanged preset rule. Desktop1366 and phone320 screenshots were inspected; other prompt/comparison/guide layouts cover 768/390 as well.

Effort remains an independent three-band lookup of each task’s own weight:1–24 minimum,25–66 steady,67–98 intense. There is no continuous effort-spent calculation or shared effort-budget simulation. The25/67 cutoffs are implementation presets, not empirical thresholds or consequences of Goodhart’s Law. Their hard24/25 display boundary is a known design limitation, explicitly documented for a separately agreed model revision.
